column1: extremity§Only in the last extremity did the crew abandon ship, and by then the deck was already under water.§直到最后的**绝境**船员才弃船，那时甲板已经没入水中。§extrem（最外，同 extreme 极端）
extroverted§The most extroverted person in the group was also the one nobody could persuade to speak on the record.§组里最**外向的**那位，也是谁也劝不动去公开发言的人。§extro（向外）+ vert（转，同 convert 转变）
exuberant§The garden is exuberant to the point of chaos, and its owner insists that is precisely the design.§这座花园**繁盛**到近乎混乱，主人坚称那正是设计本意。§ex-（出）+ uber（丰饶）→ 满溢出来
exultant§The exultant crowd stayed until midnight, and the result was overturned on a technicality nine days later.§**欢欣鼓舞的**人群待到午夜，而结果九天后因一个程序问题被推翻。§ex-（出）+ salt ← sal（跳，同 salient 突出的）→ 高兴得跳起来
exultation§Her exultation lasted about an hour, until she read the second paragraph of the acceptance letter.§她的**狂喜**持续了大约一小时，直到读了录取信的第二段。§
fabricate§Someone fabricated four of the eleven interviews, and the paper spent two years working out which four.§有人**捏造**了十一次访谈中的四次，报社花了两年弄清是哪四次。§fabric（工坊／构造，同 fabric 织物）→ 造出来
fabrication§The whole account is a fabrication, and the only true detail in it is the weather on the day described.§整段叙述都是**编造**，其中唯一真实的细节是所述那天的天气。§
facetious§His facetious answer was quoted without the smile, and it cost him an appointment he actually wanted.§他**开玩笑的**回答被引用时没带上那个笑容，害他丢了一个真心想要的职位。§
facile§The comparison is facile: two countries, one number each, and forty differences the writer ignores.§这个比较**失之浅易**——两个国家，各一个数字，还有作者忽略的四十项差异。§fac（做，同 factory 工厂）→ 做起来太容易
faintly§The signature is faintly visible under ultraviolet light, and it is not the name printed on the label.§在紫外线下签名**隐约**可见，而它并非标签上印的名字。§
fallacious§The reasoning is fallacious in a way that is hard to see and easy to repeat, which is why it spread.§这个推理的**谬误**难以察觉而易于复述，所以它传开了。§fall（欺骗，同 false 虚假的）
famish§The siege famished a city of ninety thousand, and the relief convoy arrived four days after the surrender.§围城让一座九万人的城市**忍饥挨饿**，救援车队在投降四天后才到。§
fanfare§The product launched with enormous fanfare and was withdrawn, without any announcement, nine months later.§这款产品在巨大的**喧腾造势**中上市，九个月后悄无声息地撤市。§
fastidious§A fastidious editor caught eleven inconsistencies that four earlier readers had walked straight past.§一位**挑剔的**编辑逮到十一处前后矛盾，而此前四位读者径直走了过去。§
fathom§Nobody could fathom why the machine failed only on Tuesdays until someone checked the cleaning schedule.§没人**弄明白**为什么机器只在周二出故障，直到有人查了保洁排班。§
felicitous§The title was felicitous: three words that told you the subject, the argument, and the author's attitude.§这个标题**恰到好处**——三个词就告诉你主题、论点和作者的态度。§felic（幸运／恰当，同 felicity 幸福）
feral§The feral population descended from four abandoned pets and now numbers in the thousands.§这个**野化的**种群源自四只被遗弃的宠物，如今数以千计。§fer（野兽，同 ferocious 凶猛的）
fertilize§Farmers fertilize the field every autumn, and the runoff has been feeding an algal bloom downstream for a decade.§农民每年秋天给这块地**施肥**，径流十年来一直在滋养下游的藻华。§fert（携带／多产，同 fertile 肥沃的）
fervent§Her fervent defense of the programme was more persuasive than the evaluation, which nobody read.§她对这个项目**热切的**辩护比评估报告更有说服力，而报告没人读。§ferv（沸腾，同 fervor 热情）
feverish§A feverish week of rewriting produced the chapter she had failed to write in the previous four months.§一周**狂热的**改写产出了她此前四个月没能写出的那一章。§
fickle§Funding here is fickle, and a laboratory can lose in one committee meeting what it built over nine years.§这里的经费**变幻无常**，一个实验室可能在一次委员会会议上失去九年积累。§
fictional§The town is fictional and the road, the church, and the bakery in it are all recognizable to anyone local.§这座镇子是**虚构的**，而书中的路、教堂和面包房，本地人一眼都认得出。§
fidelity§The translator chose fidelity over elegance, and the result reads awkwardly and argues correctly.§译者选择了**忠实**而非优雅，结果读来别扭而论证准确。§fid（信任，同 confide 吐露）
figurative§The phrase is figurative in the original and was translated literally, which is how the confusion began.§这个短语在原文中是**比喻性的**，却被直译了，混乱由此开始。§figur（形状，同 figure 图形）
filial§Filial duty kept her in the town for eleven years, and she has never once described it as a sacrifice.§**子女的**责任把她留在镇上十一年，而她从未把这形容为牺牲。§fil（儿女）
finagle§He finagled a seat on the committee by volunteering for the one task nobody else would take.§他靠主动承担一件没人肯干的活儿，**弄到**了委员会的一个席位。§
finesse§The repair required finesse rather than force: a quarter turn, in the right direction, at the right temperature.§这次维修需要的是**巧劲**而非蛮力——在合适的温度下，朝对的方向转四分之一圈。§
fiscal§The fiscal year ends in March, which is why every department spends its remaining budget in February.§**财政**年度三月结束，所以每个部门都在二月花光剩余预算。§fisc（国库）
fitful§His sleep was fitful for nine weeks, and the doctor treated everything except the noise from the road.§他的睡眠**断断续续**了九周，医生什么都治了，就是没管路上的噪音。§fit（阵发）
flabbergast§The size of the bill flabbergasted a family that had been told the procedure was covered.§账单的金额**惊呆**了一家被告知这项手术在保险范围内的人。§
flagrant§The breach was flagrant enough that the regulator acted within a week, which almost never happens.§这次违规**明目张胆**到监管方一周内就出手，这几乎从未发生过。§flagr（燃烧，同 conflagration 大火）→ 火烧火燎地显眼
flamboyance§The flamboyance of the design hides a plan of remarkable economy: four rooms and one staircase.§设计的**华丽炫目**掩盖了一个异常经济的平面——四个房间和一道楼梯。§flamb（火焰，同 flame 火焰）
flank§Cavalry attacked the flank while the infantry held the centre, and the whole line collapsed in an hour.§骑兵攻击**侧翼**而步兵守住中路，整条战线在一小时内崩溃。§
flatter§The photograph flatters the building: it hides the car park and the four storeys added in 1978.§这张照片**美化**了这栋楼——它藏起了停车场和 1978 年加建的四层。§
flaunt§She flaunted the credential in every meeting until someone finally asked where she had earned it.§她在每次会议上**炫耀**这份资历，直到终于有人问起她是在哪儿拿到的。§
flaw§The flaw was in the specification, not the workmanship, and it took nine failures to find it.§缺陷在于规格书而非工艺，找到这个**瑕疵**花了九次故障。§
flimsy§The evidence was flimsy and the conviction stood for twenty-two years before the appeal succeeded.§证据**站不住脚**，而这项定罪维持了二十二年才上诉成功。§
flippant§A flippant remark in a private message became the headline, and the apology took four days to write.§私信里一句**轻佻的**话成了新闻标题，道歉写了四天。§
flora§The flora of the island includes nine species found nowhere else, and four of them grow on one cliff.§这座岛的**植物群**包括九个别处没有的物种，其中四种长在同一处崖壁上。§Flora（罗马花神）
florid§His florid prose was fashionable in 1890 and is the main reason nobody reads him now.§他**辞藻华丽的**文风在 1890 年是时髦，也是如今没人读他的主要原因。§flor（花，同 floral 花的）
floridity§The floridity of the decoration exhausts the eye long before you reach the room it was built to lead into.§装饰的**繁缛**在你走到它本要引向的房间之前就已让眼睛疲惫。§
flotilla§A flotilla of small boats evacuated four thousand people in a night that no plan had anticipated.§一支小船**船队**在无人预料的一夜里疏散了四千人。§flota（船队）+ -illa（小）
flotsam§Flotsam from the wreck washed ashore for nine months, and each piece was catalogued by a local teacher.§沉船的**漂浮残骸**冲上岸持续了九个月，每一件都由一位本地教师编目。§
flounder§The presentation floundered from the second slide onward, and he never recovered the room's attention.§这场演示从第二张幻灯片起就**乱了阵脚**，他再没能拉回全场的注意力。§
foible§Everyone tolerated the foible until it turned out to be the reason four invoices had gone unpaid.§人人都容忍这个**小毛病**，直到发现它正是四张发票未付的原因。§
foil§The quiet assistant is the foil for a boss whose confidence would otherwise be unbearable to watch.§这位安静的助理是老板的**衬托**，否则老板的自信会让人看不下去。§
fondness§Her fondness for the old system was practical, not sentimental: it had never once lost a record.§她对旧系统的**偏爱**是务实而非念旧的——它一次也没丢过记录。§
foolhardy§The crossing was foolhardy rather than brave, and two of the four who attempted it did not return.§这次穿越是**有勇无谋**而非勇敢，四名尝试者中有两人没有回来。§fool（傻）+ hardy（勇）
forage§Bees forage up to four miles from the hive, which is why one field of spray can empty a distant apiary.§蜜蜂在离蜂箱四英里内**觅食**，所以一块喷药的田能清空一处远方的蜂场。§
forbearance§His forbearance lasted through nine months of missed payments and ended with a single letter.§他的**克制忍耐**熬过了九个月的欠款，最后以一封信告终。§for-（放弃）+ bear（承受）
forego§She agreed to forego the fee entirely, and the case that resulted set a precedent worth far more.§她同意完全**放弃**这笔费用，由此产生的案例开创了价值高得多的先例。§
forerunner§The 1911 machine was the forerunner of everything in this room, and it worked on exactly the same principle.§1911 年的那台机器是这屋里一切的**先驱**，其原理完全相同。§fore（在前）+ runner（跑者）
foreshadow§The opening paragraph foreshadows the ending so plainly that a careful reader can guess it in a minute.§开头一段如此明白地**预示**了结局，细心的读者一分钟就能猜到。§fore（在前）+ shadow（影子）
foresight§The foresight to buy that land in 1962 is now credited to a committee that voted against it twice.§1962 年买下那块地的**远见**，如今被归功于一个曾两次投票反对的委员会。§fore（在前）+ sight（看见）
forestall§A single memo forestalled a strike that four months of negotiation had failed to prevent.§一份备忘录**先发制人地阻止**了一场四个月谈判都没能避免的罢工。§fore（在前）+ stall（摊位）→ 抢先摆摊拦住
forfeit§They forfeited the deposit rather than sign a lease that ran nine years with no exit clause.§他们宁可**丧失**押金，也不签一份长达九年、没有退出条款的租约。§for-（外）+ fait ← fac（做）→ 做错而丧失
forgettable§The film is forgettable and profitable, and the studio has since made four more exactly like it.§这部电影**令人过目即忘**却赚钱，制片厂此后又拍了四部一模一样的。§
forgivable§The first mistake was forgivable; repeating it after the review had named it was not.§第一次失误是**可原谅的**，在评审已经点名之后再犯就不是了。§
forgo§He forgoes the salary and takes a share instead, which has made him either rich or ridiculous depending on the year.§他**放弃**薪水改拿股份，这让他要么富有要么可笑，全看是哪一年。§
formality§The vote was a formality: the decision had been taken in a corridor two hours earlier.§这次表决只是**走个形式**——决定两小时前在走廊里就做出了。§form（形式）
formidable§She is a formidable questioner, and witnesses have learned to answer only what she actually asked.§她是个**令人生畏的**提问者，证人们学会了只回答她真正问的问题。§formid（恐惧）
formulaic§The plot is formulaic and the dialogue is not, and the second fact keeps the series on air.§情节是**套路化的**而对白不是，后一点让这部剧集得以续播。§
formulate§It took the team nine months to formulate a single question that the data they had could actually answer.§团队花了九个月才**明确表述**出一个他们手上数据真正能回答的问题。§formul（公式，同 formula 公式）
forsake§He forsook a secure post for a project that failed twice before it worked, and it worked spectacularly.§他**舍弃**了稳妥的职位去做一个失败两次才成的项目，而它成得辉煌。§for-（完全）+ sake（争执）→ 撇下不管
fortify§Two extra beams fortified a floor that had been carrying twice its designed load for eleven years.§两根额外的梁**加固**了一层楼板，它已超设计荷载一倍承重了十一年。§fort（强，同 fortress 要塞）
fortuitous§The meeting was fortuitous and consequential: they queued for the same coffee and founded a company.§这次相遇是**偶然的**却意义重大——他们排队买同一杯咖啡，然后创办了一家公司。§fortuit（机遇，同 fortune 运气）
founder§The scheme foundered on a detail nobody had checked: the site had no legal access road.§这个方案**触礁失败**于一个没人核查过的细节——那块地没有合法的通行道路。§fund（底部，同 foundation 地基）→ 沉到底
fragility§The fragility of the network was invisible until one cable failed and took nine services with it.§这个网络的**脆弱**在一根线缆故障并带垮九项服务之前无从察觉。§frag（破碎，同 fracture 骨折）
